title: What I learned building a 300 level tower defense with Claude Code
author: BrownaroStudios
selftext:
Maze Warden TD is a tower defense where there's no fixed road. You place the walls yourself, so the enemies walk whatever route you leave them and your towers sit along it. The game won't let you block the path completely, so the puzzle is making it as long as you can while keeping it open. The clip is the first two waves of a run: a few walls to bend the lane, a couple of towers, and the creeps walking it. The rest of the maze is up to you.

**How we built it:** Godot 4, and Claude Code writes most of the code. I do the design, play every build and decide what stays. A few things that actually worked for us:

1. Have it write tests that play the game, not just tests for functions. When we added levels 201 to 300, Claude wrote a headless script that plays every one of those levels start to finish in the real game scene and checks every wave resolves, the level unlocks the next one, and each new mechanic shows up on the wave it should. All 100 passed before I ever opened them on a phone. That's what made adding 100 levels at once feel safe.
2. Point it at your analytics. Our mid-run bonus chest was offered over 1,300 times in a week to a handful of players and nobody ever watched the ad for it. Claude pulled that out of Firebase, and the fix was to change the reward, not the button. Next update the chest opens a little window where you pick Warden Marks, an extra life or gold.
3. Make difficulty something you can test. We added Warden's Aid: if a level beats you three times in a row it offers to take some health off the enemies for that attempt, and your stars still count. It's a few lines of rules, so it's easy to check and easy to tune.

**On art:** we started with AI sprites. The gameplay art (towers, creatures, terrain, effects) is now a Craftpix asset kit, and the app icon and some menu icons are still made in Recraft. Music and sound effects are CC0.

It's free on iOS and Android if you want to see it in action:

[Maze Warden on iOS](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6786962545)  
[Maze Warden on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.brownaro.mazewardentd)

Happy to answer anything about the workflow. What do you use to test your games when AI is writing most of the code?
